paper_title: Nuclear decay anomalies as a signature of axion dark matter
suggested_experiment_name: JRC Tritium decay (3H nuclear decay anomaly search)
coupling_convention: 1/f_a in GeV^-1 as plotted on the y-axis (x-axis is m_a in eV); NOT converted to f_a
notes: Paper analyzes 12 years of JRC 3H (tritium) decay data for oscillations induced by QCD axion DM via time-varying theta-angle affecting nuclear binding energies. Main measured result is directly on the f_a-m_a plane (Fig. 3 plots 1/f_a vs m_a), so AxionMass is appropriate. Only endpoint values are given explicitly in text: f_a > 9.4e12 GeV at m_a = 1.7e-23 eV down to f_a > 1.8e10 GeV at m_a = 8.7e-21 eV (95% CL). Intermediate points interpolated using the fa ∝ 1/ma scaling implied by the signal amplitude I ∝ 1/(ma^2 fa^2), which is consistent with the stated endpoints. Assumes rho_DM = 0.45 GeV/cm^3. Paper also presents future sensitivity projections (fa up to 1.5e16 GeV) which are NOT included in data_points. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.85, 35)) | Vision: Figure 3 plots m_a [eV] (x, 1e-25 to 1e-12) vs 1/f_a [GeV^-1] (y, 1e-22 to 1e-2). The paper's own 95% CL exclusion (Tritium decay, dark red) is anchored by explicit caption values: f_a < 9.4e12 GeV at m_a = 1.7e-23 eV and f_a < 1.8e10 GeV at m_a = 8.7e-21 eV, i.e. 1/f_a from 1.06e-13 to 5.6e-11 GeV^-1. Interior points follow the slope-1 log-log scaling (1/f_a ∝ m_a) implied by I ∝ 1/(m_a f_a)^2 and confirmed by the plotted diagonal boundary; small periodogram wiggles are not resolvable at this image scale. Signal frequency is 2x axion frequency (cos 2ωt), consistent with the quoted frequency range 8.0e-9–4.2e-6 Hz. ρ_DM = 0.45 GeV/cm^3 assumed.
